subject: The savings sermon, and a long queue of cars on the road
alt: Satish Acharya’s cartoon: at the upper left is the face of an elderly man with a white beard, round glasses and a brown sleeveless jacket, with one hand on his chest, saying, ‘WE DON’T BELIEVE IN KHAO, PIYO, MAUJ KARO!’ At the upper right the same man sits in a blue car wrapped in a thick saffron garland, one finger raised ahead. Behind him a long line of dark blue cars winds down the road. At the lower right stands an ordinary man in a pink shirt and blue jeans, a brown bag on his shoulder and a green shopping bag in his hand; he stares at the queue in alarm, and his speech bubble reads, ‘ASK THAT MAN TO SAVE!’ Satish Acharya’s signature is at the lower right.
chutki: The prime minister says India does not believe in ‘khao, piyo, mauj karo’ and that people should save. Yet his own convoy holds up the road with a long queue of cars. The ordinary man with a shopping bag below says exactly this: ‘Ask that man to save!’

The needle is that the sermon on saving is aimed at the man who already has a queue of cars, while the man who should be asked to save stands there with a bag. When power begins to save with its own convoy, the ordinary man will not need the sermon.
